## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kosiyajātaka* (Ja 226) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The framing narrative is set at Jetavana and concerns the King of Kosala, who set out to suppress a border uprising at an improper season of the year (*akāle nikkhami*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. 

Opening with the verse line *Kāle nikkhamanā sādhu* ("There is a time"), the Buddha recounts a story of the past in which a king acted rashly until persuaded to turn back by the counsel of his wise minister (*paṇḍitāmacca*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the king of that past era was reborn as Ānanda, while the wise counselor was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879].

Neither curated parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan nor automated text reuses are listed on SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
